ubi176_broken_vendor_links_2026_08_23.note: UBI-176: docs-vendor description text carries real markdown links written relative to cloud.google.com/registry.terraform.io -- correct on the vendor's own site, but resolving as broken root-relative paths on this one. Live count, not the quoted estimate: 187 occurrences across 127 fields (83 distinct URL targets), all source=docs-vendor, 0 from any other source. Fixed by rewriting to absolute vendor URLs (prepending https://cloud.google.com), not stripping. Two real, separate data-quality issues found and fixed along the way, both live-verified before applying: a stray trailing quote character baked into the original extracted vendor text (google_apigee_apidoc's own image_url field, .../portal-files") and a real, unfilled Google API doc template variable (`{$api_version}`, google_deploymentmanager_deployment.operation, 3 occurrences) -- substituted with `v1`, Compute Engine's real, current stable API version, both confirmed live-resolving after the fix. 12 of the 83 URLs (google_ml_job/model/version -- the legacy AI Platform/ML Engine API) point at real Google documentation that has since been fully retired -- confirmed live: every real /ai-platform/ candidate replacement path tried redirects to the same generic product hub, not specific content -- left pointing at their real, literal, absolute vendor path rather than a misleading generic redirect; a genuine, separate vendor-side content-retirement limitation, not further fixable from this side without fabricating a wrong link. Fixed in two places: artifacts/gcp/descriptions.json itself (the durable record) AND the 31 already-published .mdx pages directly (regen_pages.py's own injection pipeline reads docs-vendor text straight from the raw dump-ir schema at generation time, not from descriptions.json, so the artifact fix alone would not have propagated to already-generated pages without either a full corpus regen or this direct patch -- confirmed live: 193 occurrences found baked directly into 31 published pages, patched with the identical fix rules). One further real bug caught mid-fix: MDX escapes literal curly braces as HTML entities in body text (`{` -> `{`), so the {$api_version} fix's plain string replace silently missed its one occurrence inside an already-published page (google_deploymentmanager_deployment) until checked and fixed directly. Verified: 0 root-relative markdown links remain in any GCP descriptions.json docs-vendor entry or any published GCP page, mint validate passes.

ubi180_uppercase_local_name_2026_08_23.note: UBI-180: ubx sdk gen (sdk/codegen/templates/{go,py,ts}) rejected google_siteverification's own real resource -- its raw typeName carried a literal capital, google_siteverification_siteVerification_web_resource, from ubx-provider-dynamic's own discoverydoc.go inserting the live Discovery Document's own doc.Name field (Google's real, live value for this one API is "siteVerification", mixed case) directly into the typeName, unlike the resource-tree key two lines above it, which already went through the identical real ToSnakeCase conversion (a prior, already-fixed instance of this exact bug class). Decided to normalize at the source (doc.Name now gets the same ToSnakeCase treatment), not accept-and-escape per language -- the established design precedent (the sibling resource-tree-key fix, and this project's own standing 'never a best-effort coercion, refuse loudly instead' doctrine, docs/sdk.md row 5) already treats camelCase-to-snake_case as a real, deterministic, single-source normalization, not a guess; three separate per-language escape implementations would triple the maintenance surface and risk the three languages silently disagreeing on the resulting identifier. Swept all 468 real, top-level configured dynamic providers (not the inflated 474 count, which included [dynamic_providers.<name>.auth] TOML sub-tables) via a real --dump-ir run BEFORE fixing -- google_siteverification was the ONLY resource anywhere with an uppercase-carrying WireType or localName; every other provider's own typeName-synthesis path (resourcemap.go for OpenAPI/Kubernetes/GitHub/Datadog/Azure, cloudformation.go's own Resolve for AWS) was independently confirmed to already run every input through its own real ToSnakeCase/toSnakeCase before it ever reaches a typeName. Fixed upstream, verified live: go/py/ts codegen all succeed now (previously a hard crash, exit code 2). Real typeName: google_siteverification_site_verification_web_resource (the word-boundary underscore ToSnakeCase inserts means this does NOT collapse under gcp_corrected_key's own doubling-collapse pattern, which requires an exact, case-sensitive prefix match -- a real, separate, minor naming quirk, not a bug, left as-is). Two stale, pre-existing artifact entries (google_siteVerification_web_resource -- mixed case -- and google_siteverification_web_resource -- no underscore -- neither matching the real, now-confirmed key) found and cleaned up: real, correctly-extracted content moved to the real key rather than re-researched from scratch.
